name: Gecko colour camera
description: A small colour camera. From 500 km each pixel covers 39 m of ground and one pass sees a strip 80 km wide.
why_it_matters: It is light and needs little power. It records only red, green and blue light, like a phone camera.
limitation: Sees only red, green and blue light. Measuring plant health needs near-infrared light too.
estimate_basis: Cost: no public price; placeholder of US$30,000, close to the top of the only public CubeSat camera price found (XCAM C3D, US$11,900 to 27,400, FY2022, satcatalog.com). Data rate: not published; derived as pixels across (80 km / 39 m = 2,051) x 10 bits x lines per second (ground speed 7.06 km/s at 500 km / 39 m). Mass and power are the published upper limits (below 0.5 kg, below 6 W).

name: MultiScape50 multispectral camera
description: A camera that records eight colour bands, from blue to near-infrared. From 500 km each pixel covers 30 m of ground and one pass sees a strip 120 km wide.
why_it_matters: Healthy plants reflect a lot of near-infrared light, so this camera can measure plant health. Its wide view covers the Earth quickly, but the detail is modest.
estimate_basis: Cost: no public price and no close public comparison; US$100,000 is a placeholder set by the game team. Data rate: not published; derived as 4,096 pixels across x 12 bits x 8 bands x lines per second (ground speed 7.06 km/s at 500 km / 30 m), with no compression.

name: MultiScape100 multispectral camera
description: A larger telescope with the same eight colour bands. From 500 km each pixel covers 4.75 m of ground, but one pass sees a strip only 19.4 km wide.
why_it_matters: Very sharp pictures show single fields and roads. The narrow view means covering the whole Earth takes far longer, and the sharp pictures produce much more data.
estimate_basis: Cost: no public price and no close public comparison; US$250,000 is a placeholder set by the game team. Data rate: not published; derived as 4,096 pixels across x 12 bits x 8 bands x lines per second (ground speed 7.06 km/s at 500 km / 4.75 m), with no compression.
